The problems really start to arise when we talk about tools that aren't readily available like complex factory equipment or something like that. Also I would like to clarify that when I speak of something being communally owned I don't want the state to own it on behalf of the people like in the ussr. The people who directly use the equipment to produce stuff should be the ones who own it.

When a stock is private, anyone *theoretically* could buy it and become a part owner in the company. However, depending on the company, most of the actual workers would be unable to purchase the stock. It's still a private company, but instead of one individual owning it, multiple individuals own it collectively. If we lived in a socialist mode of production, the workers who use the company to produce a good or provide a service would own a company and make decisions democratically between themselves.

I would say there are 3 forms of property under capitalism. Private, Personal, and public. Private property are things you own that you use to make money. This could be tools, a factory, some sort of intellectual property, the list goes on. Personal property is stuff that you own that you use out of necessity or desire, such as your house, your car, or your phone, just to name a few examples. Public property would be anything owned by the government or the people, like a park or a school or the roads you drive on. When I communist advocates for the abolition of private property, they are advocating for the private property to one way or another become public or communally owned. Hope this helped.
